method: web tool opened primary papers and official documentation; statements below are paraphrases, teaching choices or labeled inferences

sources.title: Bigtable, OSDI2006
supports: §2/§3 sorted row keys, tablet row ranges and single-row atomic read/modify/write, not general cross-row transactions
§6 Bloom filters check row/column membership in SSTables
column qualifiers versus cell timestamp versions
sources.scope: original paper model, not all current wide-row product APIs

sources.title: Dynamo, SOSP2007
supports: §4.6 sloppy operations use first N healthy nodes, with hinted handoff
single-key versions and application reconciliation trade consistency for availability
§6.1 optional buffered writes trade durability for latency; W replies alone need not be durable
sources.inference: the explicit W={N1,N4},R={N2,N3} schedule is this chapter's witness, not quoted experimental data

sources.title: Spanner, OSDI2012
supports: external consistency uses transaction ordering and TrueTime commit wait
sources.scope: one implementation, not a universal requirement to use TrueTime

sources.title: Dremel, PVLDB2010
supports: read-only nested data, column-striped representation and execution-tree aggregation
data can be read in situ from existing storage
sources.scope: the paper's query path does not imply every columnar database lacks transactions; numeric bytes are our assumptions

sources.title: O'Neil et al., LSM-tree, 1996
supports: memory/disk components defer and batch changes through rolling merges
§2.2 exact and range finds search components; point finds can pay more I/O than B-tree
cached B-tree upper pages and workload assumptions affect costs
sources.scope: not a claim that every current LSM has the original paper's exact layout

sources.title: One Size Fits All, ICDE2005
supports: different workload classes can benefit from different engine organization
sources.inference: shortlist by access constraints; the chapter does not prescribe a new system per table

sources.title: PostgreSQL18 WAL introduction
supports: log records must be durable before corresponding persistent data pages
commit need not flush all data pages

sources.title: PostgreSQL18 Log-shipping standby servers
supports: async shipping retains acknowledged-write loss window after catastrophic primary failure
§26.2.8 distinguishes received/remote_write/durable replay and remote_apply
safe failover and replication placement must satisfy the claimed failure scope
sources.scope: the chapter's one-second list freshness and RPO requirements are assumptions, not product defaults

sources.title: RocksDB Write Stalls
supports: immutable memtable, L0 count and pending compaction thresholds can slow or stop writes
compaction backlog affects read and space amplification

sources.title: S3 conditional writes
supports: If-None-Match:* prevents overwrite of an existing current object version
conditional headers do not create a metadata-database transaction
sources.scope: immutable object IDs, namespace binding and no-key-reuse/IAM rules are explicit teaching design requirements

sources.title: S3 upload integrity
supports: checksums can be stored and independently verified
ETag is not universally a full-object MD5, especially across upload/encryption modes

sources.title: PostgreSQL18 Transaction Isolation
supports: Read Committed sees a query-start snapshot
concurrent UPDATE waits then rechecks WHERE on the updated row
repeatable-read snapshots differ from fresh query snapshots
sources.scope: we did not run PostgreSQL; the executable fixture uses actual SQLite one-writer semantics

sources.title: SQLite transactions
supports: BEGIN IMMEDIATE starts a writer immediately; one concurrent writer per database
retained read transaction sees its historic snapshot
errors/COMMIT BUSY require explicit transaction-state handling

sources.title: SQLite RETURNING
supports: RETURNING since3.35.0 returns rows changed by a statement
RETURNING does not by itself mean the transaction committed

sources.title: SQLite3.38.0 release
supports: unixepoch() introduced in3.38.0

sources.title: RocksDB Basic Operations / Synchronous Writes
supports: default non-sync write reaches OS before return, but machine crash may lose recent updates
sync=true waits for persistent storage
disableWAL changes process-crash recovery scope

sources.title: RocksDB WAL lifecycle
supports: WAL restores memtable state on recovery
retain WAL until relevant column families flush beyond its records

sources.title: PostgreSQL18 multicolumn indexes
supports: leading equalities followed by an inequality limit a multicolumn B-tree scan

teachingChoices: A1-A12 are all teaching assumptions; recomputed in ch37-numeric-review.json
CAS proof must bind full authenticated session/object identity; exact HEAD and immutable namespace enforcement remain external
exact SUM requires a trusted complete/disjoint immutable manifest and correct worker sums; hash checks alone do not prove arithmetic
tombstone visibility/recovery constraints follow from not reviving older values; real per-product GC/repair policy must be specified
